Replay

Replay Cavecrawl

9 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Implemented gameplayComparison and intentional differencesBrowser authority migration

This is a separate, in-progress reimplementation of the original Cavecrawl. Both projects remain independently runnable. The new version keeps mutable gameplay state in a World value. Replay's runner schedules simulation steps and manages input and history; replay/godot.Session connects that runtime to Godot and the network. Godot scenes display the resulting state and effects.

The online party menu creates and joins rooms through a standalone service, persists credentials, selects trusted successors automatically and rejoins recent parties. It has native TLS and browser RTC acceptance; public deployment remains open.

From the repository root:

Shell
# Open the connection menu; choose Solo, Host, Join, or a native saved run.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/play.sh

# Listen host and a client, from separate terminals.
REPLAY_CAVE_ROLE=host nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/play.sh
REPLAY_CAVE_ROLE=client nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/play.sh

# Pure gameplay tests, then real Godot solo/co-op acceptance.
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_cave/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/network_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/replication_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/save_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/recovery_run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_migration/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_migration/crash_run.sh

WASD/arrows move, E uses nearby objects, Space/click throws, Q drops the first bag slot, R heals, G sets down the relic, F pings your position, Tab holds the scoreboard, Enter focuses chat, and F5 saves the authority's game. Roles are solo, host, server, client, and observer. REPLAY_CAVE_ADDRESS, REPLAY_CAVE_PORT, REPLAY_CAVE_TOKEN (test identity), and receive-delay REPLAY_CAVE_LATENCY configure local runs. The co-op test uses 120 ms receive delay on each process. Opening the project without a role opens the connection menu. REPLAY_CAVE_LOBBY=1 enables staging for explicit launch roles.

Save files default to this project's user://cave.replay; set REPLAY_CAVE_SAVE to use another path. Launch with REPLAY_CAVE_RESUME=1 to resume as solo/host/server. The host/solo profile must be the same one that owns the saved seat. Profiles default to user://<role>.token, or an explicit REPLAY_CAVE_PROFILE path. Give each local player a distinct profile when running several clients on one machine. Keep the token file alongside your save when moving your own game to another machine; the checkpoint contains hashes rather than the credentials themselves. Original Cavecrawl saves/profiles are separate and are never read or changed. Browser saves use the token-scoped IndexedDB slot described below.

Direct Session save/resume advances the authority epoch. Clients in that profile set REPLAY_CAVE_EPOCH to the printed epoch and reuse their profile. The Room flow below follows coordinator-approved authority changes automatically; the separate direct co-op recovery fixture restarts both runtime processes. Pending actions in a loaded save are explicitly retired; already executed actions keep their deduplication frontier. See the recovery contract.

The replication gate keeps the host and guest playing while periodic authority checkpoints use their existing ENet connection. It opts the guest into backups with REPLAY_CAVE_BACKUP=1 and explicitly selects seat 2 through backup_to. It verifies a shared checkpoint containing the looted gems and open door under 120 ms receive delay, 20 ms jitter, 10% loss, and 10% duplication. General live runs also accept REPLAY_CAVE_JITTER, REPLAY_CAVE_LOSS, and REPLAY_CAVE_DUPLICATE (loss/duplication values are per 10,000). This is replication; that gate does not itself invoke takeover. The separate migration gates below do.

The native coordinator-driven room profile now supports planned handoff and crash takeover while guests keep running. Its fixture starts a coordinator, host, successor, and guest. The guest keeps its loot and performs a fresh action after reconnecting in epoch 2; planned handoff also rejoins the old host as a player. The game shows reconnect/host-change feedback and reports known rollback.

The fixture supplies REPLAY_CAVE_COORD_PORT, REPLAY_CAVE_MEMBER, REPLAY_CAVE_INCARNATION, and a 64-character lowercase hex REPLAY_CAVE_COORD_KEY. This example currently uses explicit local provisioning for room 44; use the generic Room API for other coordinator addresses/configurations. The game now has a party lobby; public account/room provisioning and the remaining M5 coverage are still pending.

Implemented gameplay#

  • The two authored floor layouts, chest stocks, den positions, wave counts, and wave rests from the original game.
  • 120 px/s movement and a 20 Hz simulation matching the original gameplay timing.
  • Six-slot bags, chest transfers, drop/grab pickups, and range-gated doors.
  • Atomic relic carry/set-down state and a version counter for carrier changes. C6 relic rules preserve it across floors and release it in place on restart. C7 carrier rules retain ownership through death, disconnect and recovery. C8 adoption transfers an old host’s relic to its successor.
  • Rocks, stamina, cooldowns, damage, chill, death spills, respawn, heal, and revive.
  • Dweller chase/flee/bite behavior, frame-owned wave/respawn clocks, floor changes, and the final escape condition.
  • Replayable pool lifetime and generation-preserving floor teardown.
  • Rock presentation: centered glyphs and bounded motion between simulation ticks, preserving simulation collision and impact timing.
  • Combat feedback: journal-driven player/dweller death bursts, player hit sparks and flashes, with correction/cancellation and detached lifetime.
  • Host moderation: remove a selected player and block rejoin, with coordinator-durable successor exclusion in Room sessions.
  • Solo, listen-host, dedicated authority, client prediction, and observer modes through replay/godot.Session.

The pure tests cover item conservation/capacity, interactions, combat/revive, floor progression, old-handle rejection, rift navigation, and the real cave model contesting loot through the network runner under loss. Godot tests now include a full co-op campaign: inventory handoff, relic carry, death/revive/respawn, stale pickup rejection, healing, all four waves and final escape with a shared victory-frame hash. Normal and faulted runs pass. This still does not establish complete authored/visual feature parity.

Comparison and intentional differences#

The static levels/level_*.tscn files are byte-for-byte copies of the original authored scenes. Entity views retain the original scene presentation while their old script attachments are removed. assets.md records source paths and hashes. The original scripts/framework are not imported into gameplay.

The new model keeps all mutable gameplay state inside World. A chest transfer updates both the chest and bag directly in one action. Projectiles, AI clocks, status effects, and entity existence participate in replay. The original uses owner-streamed movement and several authority-only consequences.

Known differences/gaps:

  • This profile keeps server-simulated movement/relic state. The separate owner-motion variant now reuses this gameplay with versioned pose producers, scoped command origins, native/Chrome recovery and a matched quiet comparison. Broader remote presentation and full parity remain work.
  • Dweller pathing uses a pure visibility graph around the authored rectangular rift. The original queries Godot's navigation mesh. Exact paths are not claimed identical; this is an explicit physics/navigation port cost to compare.
  • Floor resources and markers are captured as saved world values; seeded decorative scatter matches the original integer recipe. See authoring.md for validation, local scene assets and explicit conversion of earlier Replay saves.
  • Relic races now reject the losing action; the original consequence could accept a harmless no-op. Pickups retain any amount that does not fit the receiving bag.
  • Wave pacing now matches the original director in 262 native/WASM scenarios. Population beyond the fixed 16-dweller pool and broader floor-state correspondence remain separate comparison boundaries.
  • Chat/pings and a combat/loot scoreboard now use the optional Comms service. Party names and readiness are replayable, with native/IndexedDB local name preferences. Score latency and stamped ping names now have native/browser rename/rejoin/migration acceptance. Public provisioning, Steam paths, richer effects, and the full migration failure matrix remain open. The full old cave_test.gd scenario inventory has not been ported yet.

See parity.md and the repository roadmap.

Browser authority migration#

nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/web_run.sh builds the real Cavecrawl project and a native SQLite-backed control/signaling fixture. Three independent Chrome processes collect loot, replicate an approved checkpoint and complete planned or killed-host migration. The guest retains its inventory/seat and performs a newly accepted door action; planned mode rejoins the old host. The default matrix includes planned, crash, repeat, partition, successor_loss, return and signaling. Use RCB_MODES to select cases. Logs are retained at the printed path (RCB_LOGS overrides it).

Browser launch uses lowercase URL equivalents of REPLAY_CAVE_* options, including coord_url, coord_key, member, incarnation, token and role. These fixture credentials demonstrate the protocol; they are not public account provisioning. Room combines WebSocket control, challenged RTC signaling and direct gameplay channels. Its native endpoint encoding is unchanged; RTC destinations are explicit provider/code targets derived from the authenticated authority view.

Each run also records driver timestamps and a timing summary; these include waiting for leases and fresh browser startup that the local Room timer can omit. The signaling case drops host/client signaling sockets, verifies unchanged connection generations and epoch, and performs a new accepted game action. TLS/TURN, richer browser workloads and other browser/OS combinations remain open. See the browser migration work.

Set the scene’s debug_enabled inspector property or launch with REPLAY_DEBUG=1 for the local diagnostic overlay. F8 toggles the panel and F9 explicitly audits recent replayable history. It is disabled by default.

Run the full host/client/observer campaign with nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/campaign_run.sh.

nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/social_run.sh checks chat submission through the actual input signal, typing without moving/firing, late-join scrollback, transient ping expiry and live scoreboard loot. Chat is ephemeral session history; it is not part of a gameplay save.

nix develop --command bash tests/replay_migration/social_run.sh adds chat before and after planned/crash migration. RCB_SOCIAL=1 enables the corresponding chat, ping and scoreboard assertions in the real-browser migration gate (select RCB_MODES='planned crash'). Lobby names, stamped social names and per-player latency columns have separate native/browser acceptance; broader social UX remains open.

Run nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/social_web_run.sh for the registered browser social/migration gate.

The party lobby stores names, readiness and a party leader in World. Ready up, then let the leader press Start. Recorded departures select the lowest present seat as a new leader; reconnecting players ready again before a staged run. During play, Escape opens the party/Leave panel. After victory, Another run resets the cave/inventory while retaining profiles and cumulative stats.

REPLAY_CAVE_NAME supplies a display name. Normal native menu sessions use a stable user://player.token; existing explicit-role launch paths retain their role-specific credential defaults. Local names use user://display_name; override with REPLAY_CAVE_NAME_PATH or browser profile_namespace. REPLAY_CAVE_PERSIST=0 makes the preference session-only. Tests use isolated paths/namespaces and explicit tokens. Browser multiplayer opens through provisioned Room invite URLs; the menu offers Solo when no invite is present. Browser identities and local saves now use IndexedDB, with Resume available after a validated slot read. Public provisioning remains separate work.

Run nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/lobby_run.sh for actual menu, readiness, renaming, named chat/scoreboard, leave/reopen and native preference reload checks. The current game content is 0x4341564552504c39; see authoring.md for explicit conversion of earlier Replay saves.

Browser Solo now stores its Session identity and complete save archive in IndexedDB. The default namespace is replay-cavecrawl; profile_namespace changes it and save_slot chooses a slot (default cave). F5 or the party panel's Save run button starts a save. Wait for the completion message; Leave is disabled during the write. Resume loads and validates the saved world under the same identity and advances the authority epoch. The display name alone does not identify an owning player.

Each page retains the revision it observed before play. If another page saves first, the stale writer is refused. Leave and explicitly resume the latest save before continuing; a failed/corrupt record is never silently replaced. Room sessions keep using approved checkpoint recovery and cannot be converted into an offline save through this button. See the browser checkpoint contract.

Run nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl/browser_save_run.sh for real Chrome identity creation, forced-process recovery, exact frame restoration, stale-tab refusal and corrupt-record preservation checks. The harness uses a new isolated browser profile and dedicated test namespaces.

C5 preserves avatar health, stamina, cooldowns and active chill across descent. Initial start and Another run use explicit reset policies. See floor state and save compatibility; older Replay saves require explicit conversion.
